chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The modesty (or lowering of gaze/voice) of the maidservants is an act of nobility (karamah), and it is not from the Sunnah, nor is it an obligatory duty; and what is better than nobility?

key_terms.خَفْضُ الْجَوَارِي: Modesty or lowering of gaze/voice of maidservants

ai.seo_question: Is the modesty of maidservants an obligatory duty or just nobility in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the modest demeanor of maidservants is classified as *karamah* (nobility/elegance) rather than a strict legal obligation (*wajib*) or definitive Prophetic practice (*Sunnah*). This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on social grace and character refinement as superior voluntary virtues, distinct from the rigid boundaries of *fiqh*. The narration highlights that while not legally mandatory, cultivating such nobility is considered a higher spiritual and social ideal.
